drills.q: For each element in an array, find the first element to its right that's strictly greater, or -1 if none exists.
drills.a: Maintain a decreasing stack of indices scanning left to right; whenever the current value exceeds the stack's top, pop it and record the current value as its next-greater element.

drills.q: Given daily temperatures, return for each day how many days until a warmer temperature.
drills.a: Same decreasing-stack template as next-greater-element, but store the index gap i-j into the answer array instead of the popped element's replacement value.

drills.q: Find the largest rectangular area in a histogram of bar heights.
drills.a: Maintain an increasing stack of indices; when a shorter bar arrives, pop the top and compute area as height times width between the new stack top and current index (exclusive); append a sentinel 0 to flush remaining bars.

drills.q: Explain why a monotonic stack pass over n elements is O(n) total, not O(n^2), despite a while loop inside a for loop.
drills.a: Every index is pushed exactly once and popped at most once across the whole run; total pushes and pops are each bounded by n, so total work sums to O(n).

drills.q: Find the maximum in every sliding window of size k across an array, in O(n) total.
drills.a: Maintain a decreasing monotonic deque of indices; pop smaller elements off the back before pushing, and pop the front if it's fallen outside the window's left boundary. Front of the deque is always the current max.

drills.q: Sum the minimum of every contiguous subarray of an array, without enumerating all subarrays.
drills.a: For each element, find distances to the previous strictly-smaller and next smaller-or-equal element via monotonic stack passes; that element is the minimum for (left distance * right distance) subarrays, contributing value*left*right to the total sum.
